Locations of the Wealdwoods
Verdant Sanctuaries 
Cyclopean trees stand sentinel over the fierce winds of both field 
and ocean. The tall trees that rise between the fields of Valedayn 
and the Rhaen river host a large amount of skyelarx hollow-dens. 
From up high in these bone strewn hollows, the small winged kits 
mewl as their parents range far out to the fields south of them to 
search out freshly slain creatures from roaming packs of draffers. 
Deeper within the woods where the wind cannot be felt, bands of 
aphistus pluck fruit and seed, ever wary of getting the attention of 
a roaming jhotus, that claim the forest as their own.
The encroaching mire to the forest's south leaves little nutritional 
value in the soil for the birch tree forest to grow strong. Still these 
woods make for a safe resting point for the seasonal flights of 
drafian that glide out from the Wealdwoods to migrate to the 
fields abroad. Aphistus enjoy the relative safety of the unpopulated 
forest, nesting their young in the underbrush, their avian eyes 
watching for the sharpened mandibles of awaiting korrask that 
could violently erupt from ground.
Green Moot
Thornfen
Nearly unremarkable for its insignificant size and lack of larger 
predators, there is a hidden secret beneath the soil of this small 
forest. Just beneath the roots, a thick layer of amber rests under 
the forest floor. A Traveler could harvest great chunks of the 
ancient resin, if they're careful not to disturb the ricatrillisk and 
basilospri that keep to the canopy above.
Nestled among the foothills and steep slopes that rise to the sky-
breaking Splitspine mountain, these woods are the last haven 
of cover from the arid Grayfynn. These woods harbor denizens 
unlike many of the other Wealdwoods, as the loamy grounds 
are riddled with tunnels that lead to the limestone caverns that 
runs beneath the western side of the island. Tottering tormull 
can be found in the waning months, chewing through fallen trees 
and rotten stumps to carry the fermenting plant matter to their 
cave dwelling brood. During moonless nights, acrynn have been 
known to stalk these woods, leaping to the branches and pulling 
lexati violently from their nests.
Amberdale
In the central mountain ranges, the evergreen pines that rise 
along the snow covered slopes and granite-bare cliffs stand 
firm in the fierce winds of the peaks. Pine covered branches give 
shelter to calitross flocks that crawl over the snow swept heights 
while white-furred frondilli leap from tree to tree, drinking deep 
of the sugary sap, keeping a cautious eye on the outskirts for any 
draffers willing to enter into their woods. Closer to the peaks can 
be found the stout twisted boughs of ironwood trees, the mineral-
rich soil giving their bark a slight sheen in the wane light. While a 
rare johtus, its shaggy fur covered in pine needles, chews through 
carpets of moss that blanket the boulders that lay strewn about 
the woods.
Last Bloom
Arborn
A sprawling forest of deciduous trees spreads far and wide, grown rich from the ocean-blown western winds. With consistent rains, 
and the wetlands to the south, the Tanglewood is a forest crisscrossed with swamps and rivers. Its most prominent lake, the Rootwell, 
is a deep well of black water and is one of the best locations for fishing, as many fish unseen elsewhere live within its depths; as does 
the behemoth of an amphibian, the nuthorghull. An apex predator in its own right, capable of breaching the surface and pulling in a 
drinking aphistus with a single bite of its vast maw. To the south of these woods, willow trees rise from the drowned earth. Baughur and 
pebbleback auhk’s live in the shallow muddy waters, constantly beset by ravenous vinnirex and sacrissian. Along the western reaches 
where conifers grow in the mountain foothills, lexati soar through the branches hunting scavick. Further north past the Rootwell, the 
trees grow large, their boughs heavy with mossdown where the largest of jhotus dwell. The near endless woods capable of sustaining 
several of the far roaming apex predators, only their thunderous footfalls breaking the silence of this primordial sanctuary.
